title: Smoked Picanha Steak Platter
seoTitle: Smoked Picanha Steak Platter | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Show-stopping fat cap with smoker depth and a bright sauce
subtitle: Fat-cap Brazilian cut, coarse salt, and chimichurri for ten
description: Adapted from classic Brazilian picanha tradition (Traeger, Hey Grill Hey): picanha roasts get coarse salt, smoke at 275°F to 125°F, sear fat-side down, and slice with chimichurri for a crew platter.

steps.title: Prep picanha
steps.instruction: Score fat cap in crosshatch without cutting into meat. Coat fat cap heavily with coarse salt and pepper. Let sit 20 minutes. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Smoke at 275°F
steps.instruction: Smoke picanha fat-side up at 275°F until internal temp reaches 120–125°F, about 35–45 minutes. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Build chimichurri
steps.instruction: Pulse parsley, oregano, garlic, vinegar, oil, and pepper flakes until chunky. Rest at room temp. Plan about 8 minutes for this step at crew scale. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Sear fat cap
steps.instruction: Sear fat-side down over direct heat at 500°F+ 4–5 minutes until fat crisps and internal hits 130°F medium-rare. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Rest and slice
steps.instruction: Rest 10 minutes. Slice against the grain into 1/4-inch slices, keeping fat cap on each slice. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Hold at 170°F
steps.instruction: Arrange slices on a platter, cover loosely with foil, hold at 170°F. Serve chimichurri cold on the side. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Tonight's board
steps.instruction: Picanha platter with chimichurri, grilled limes, and farro or rice if you want starch. Cook until char marks are visible and the thickest piece reads 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground on an instant-read thermometer. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Leftovers
steps.instruction: Slice thin for steak sandwiches with chimichurri. Reheat gently at 325°F until 145°F. Plan about 8 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Salt the fat cap hard—it's the flavor engine on picanha.
Slice thin; thick slices chew tough even when temp is perfect.
Chimichurri on the side keeps bright flavor; don't cook it.
tonightSpread: Sliced picanha on a board with fat cap showing.
leftovers: Picanha bowls with rice and black beans.
Chimichurri steak wraps with pickled onion.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Picanha is the steak that looks expensive and cooks forgiving. Sliced with chimichurri, it holds at 170°F for 30 minutes without losing character.
mealPrepNotes: Score fat cap lightly before salt. Smoke whole, sear, rest 10 minutes, slice. Hold sliced beef covered at 170°F with chimichurri on the side.
